q: Osmosis differs from simple diffusion mainly because osmosis:
o: Occurs only across a semi-permeable membrane for water
why: Osmosis is water movement specifically across a semi-permeable membrane.

q: A cell placed in a hypotonic solution swells due to:
why: Water enters the cell by endosmosis when the outside solution is hypotonic.

q: Water potential is the sum of solute potential and pressure potential, written as:
why: Water potential equation: Psi(w) = Psi(s) + Psi(p).

q: If a cell has solute potential Psi(s) = -8 bar and pressure potential Psi(p) = +5 bar, its water potential Psi(w) is:
Shrinking of the protoplast away from the cell wall in a hypertonic solution is called:
why: Water loss by exosmosis causes the protoplast to shrink from the wall: plasmolysis.

q: At the endodermis of a root, the apoplast water pathway is blocked by the:
why: The Casparian strip forces water through the symplast (membrane) path at the endodermis.

q: The cohesion-tension theory explains ascent of sap mainly through:
o: Transpiration pull plus cohesion of water molecules
why: Transpiration creates tension; cohesion keeps the water column unbroken, pulling water up.

q: According to the K+ ion theory, stomata open when guard cells:
o: Lose K+ ions and become flaccid
Accumulate K+ ions and become turgid
why: K+ accumulation lowers water potential, water enters, guard cells turn turgid, pore opens.

q: Which pathway of water movement through the root cortex passes through cell walls and intercellular spaces without crossing membranes?
why: The apoplast pathway moves water through walls/intercellular spaces, not across membranes.

q: A raisin placed in plain water swells because of:
o: Endosmosis as the raisin is hypertonic to water
why: The raisin's concentrated cell contents draw in water by endosmosis, causing swelling.
